Tara (Design): Quick follow-up from the console walkthrough 1: focus outlines are inconsistent across components and some are nearly invisible in dark theme. Also screen reader testing flagged ambiguous labels in the dashboard filter bar. Screenshot: https://figma.redwood.app/dashboard-focus-grid
Marek (Frontend): I can repro the thin ring issue. We have mixed styles: some elements use outline: 1px solid var(--muted), others use box-shadow. On dark theme the 1px outline disappears.
Lina (A11y): two immediate problems: (1) focus indicator must be visible (not only color) and not rely on hover state; (2) some filter controls expose both a visible label and aria-label, causing VoiceOver to read twice. Example markup: <label>Region</label><select aria-label="Region"> -> double announce.
Omar (UX): For visuals I'd prefer keeping lightweight UI but improving accessibility without changing spacing. Can we introduce a unified focus token: 3px solid + subtle halo for dark, 2px for light?
Marek (Frontend): proposed CSS:
```
:root { --focus-thick: 3px; --focus-color: #60a5fa; }
:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-thick) solid var(--focus-color); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 6px rgba(96,165,250,0.06); }
```
Will try on select, input, button, chip.
Lina (A11y): that solves visibility. For labels: prefer aria-labelledby pattern. Keep visible label for sighted users but give it an id and set select aria-labelledby="label-id". Remove aria-label attributes to avoid duplicate accessible names. If we need SR-only extra context, add a <span class="sr-only"> that expands name to "Region filter" for screen readers.
Tara (Design): good. Also noted when keyboard tabbing through chips (tag filters) the tab order jumps unexpectedly: sometimes chips are not reachable and require arrow keys only. Users expect Tab to move between interactive controls and arrow keys for within compound widgets.
Marek (Frontend): we're currently using role="listbox" for chip groups with arrow handling (roving tabindex). That breaks typical Tab order. We should only apply roving for single-focus widget like a menu; for filter chips we want each chip to be focusable (tabindex=0) so Tab moves across them. Roving can be preserved for the internal arrow behavior if it's a true composite widget, but semantics must be clear.
Lina (A11y): exactly. If chips act like multi-select toggle buttons, use role="button" with aria-pressed="true|false" and make them tabbable. Do not hide them from the Tab order. That aligns with AT expectations.
Ben (QA): test plan: keyboard-only walkthrough (Tab/Shift+Tab) should hit: search -> filter controls -> chips -> apply button, and screen reader should announce chip state like 'Region: US, pressed'. Also run NVDA/JAWS/VO samples to confirm no double announces. Visual snapshots for focus rings in light/dark.
Marek (Frontend): I'll open a PR to: (1) standardize :focus-visible token across components; (2) switch filters to aria-labelledby; (3) make chips tabbable with aria-pressed; (4) fix select label ids. Will include before/after screenshots and VoiceOver notes.
Lina (A11y): I'll review the PR and run a quick SR smoke on mac+windows. Minor nit: ensure any sr-only text uses the .sr-only utility (not display:none) so it's in accessibility tree. Also double-check that changing focus visuals doesn't hide text outlines for high-contrast mode.
Tara (Design): owners: Marek (PR), Lina (a11y review), Ben (QA). Target: small patch this sprint. design-bot: Updated component spec and focus tokens at https://figma.redwood.app/file/focus-tokens :sparkles:
